title: Design System: Ledgendary marketing home (v3)
scope: site-v3/ only (v3 alternate): the home and the solo, team and enterprise audience pages. Not a project-wide system; site/ (v1) and site-v2/ are competing alternates in their own worlds. Derived from site-v3/styles.css, site-v3/audiences.css, the four HTML pages, site-v3/app.js and site-v3/audiences.js at 5a2fceb.

err.purpose: Refusals and invalid entries, as text, icons or a 2px ring only.

display.purpose: Hero headline only, 15ch, balanced; 3.25rem on phones.

headline.purpose: Section headings; closing call at clamp(3rem, 7vw, 5.5rem); 2.6rem on phones.

date-numeral.purpose: Scrubbed chapter's date readout in text-2; scales up to 1.3x above the pinned stage (1.25x under 1400px), 1x when pinned, unscaled 2rem at 720px and below.

figure.purpose: Received figure filling coral on Nov 18; rest date (2rem) and timesheet totals (26px, 85% width) follow the recipe.

title.purpose: Chapter story line and playbook preview name (2rem).

doc-title.purpose: Titles inside product frames and caption titles; 17px on phones in frames.

lede.purpose: Hero and section ledes in mut, 46 to 60ch, pretty wrap.

label.purpose: Table heads, panel heads, sidebar groups, demo tags; sentence case, 12 to 12.5px, 550 to 600.

icons.size: 16px default; 12 to 14px in chips and tool buttons; 18px in list leads

shadows.name: window
shadows.purpose: Every standalone window: the home books and playbook, and each feature window on the audience pages.

shadows.name: ring
shadows.purpose: Every card, control, chip and tag; replaces borders.

shadows.name: knob
shadows.purpose: Scrubber knob; as-of thumb and rest marker take the ground ring only.

shadows.name: wait-halo
shadows.purpose: Knob breathing while the invoice waits (Nov 17 to Nov 18).

shadows.name: focus
shadows.purpose: Global focus; inputs use inset 0 0 0 2px #f3efe6 instead.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing for state and entrances.

motion.name: t-state
motion.purpose: Chip, pill, sidebar, tally and slot colour changes.

motion.name: land
motion.purpose: Captions, panes, journal entries, playbook preview; activity rows drop 8px.

motion.name: climax-fill
motion.value: clip-path driven by --c (0 to 1) from scroll
motion.purpose: Received figure filling coral as Nov 18 lands.

motion.name: wait
motion.purpose: Knob halo while waiting for payment; the wink 'Wait for it…' captions the same stretch.

motion.name: scroll-weights
motion.purpose: Wait stretch and paid day scroll slowest.

motion.name: date-scale
motion.value: scale 1 + q x 0.3 (0.25 under 1400px), q from 1 at top to 0 at pin
motion.purpose: Hero date numeral settling into the readout; off at 720px and below.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: durations .01ms; stage un-pinned; Earlier/Later stepper shown
motion.purpose: State never depends on motion; no-JS shows dated static panes.

breakpoints.name: mid
breakpoints.purpose: App sidebar to 56px icon rail; stage column 260px; short event chip labels.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Activity column dropped; hero, section heads, books grid and closing call stack.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Frame un-pinned and flowing; rail chips and mid dates hidden; captions inline; figure and tally hidden; grids single column; nav 56px. Audience pages: nav links hidden (footer carries them), breadcrumbs reduced to the current item, money tables stack into labelled rows and never drop a figure, seat tabs stack avatar over name.

narrative.overview:
One evening, one ground. A deep green-black field runs edge to edge under every chapter; there are no light sections. The product is drawn in its own dark theme on that field: tonal steps of the same green (inset, panel, raised panel) separated by crisp 1px lines, with no glow, no neon edge and no glass. Warm off-white carries the text. One accent, signal coral, marks two things only: *now* (the scrubber, the current-date marker, today's column, the as-of thumb) and *settled* (Paid, the received figure, the primary button). Ink sits on coral, always.

The page is a date. The first chapter pins a product canvas under a horizontal rail from Oct 27 to Nov 18, and the canvas state is a pure function of that date: proposal, portal, timesheet and invoice panes swap as scroll moves the marker, the activity column fills, the tally and the received figure follow. A large light date numeral in the hero is the image; it settles into the chapter's readout as the stage pins. Later chapters repeat the idea at smaller scale: five seats read on Nov 18, a books window with its own date control reconstructs receivables, P&L and the journal as of any day, and the closing call ends on a rested rail at Nov 18, paid.

Type is one variable family, Bricolage Grotesque, used on its width axis: statements condensed (75 to 82%) and heavy (740 to 760), dates condensed and light (300), everything read at full width and 400 to 650. Numbers in columns and money are tabular.

The audience pages (solo, team, enterprise) carry the same idea per audience: each hero pins its own rail over any number of days (enterprise jumps nine years to 2036 across a hatched gap) with a product frame whose panes follow the date, then feature sections in which a copy column sits beside one window, a seat switcher, an as-of scrubber over a month, and a comparison table. Inside every audience window the content is rows and plain blocks under hairlines, never boxes inside the box.
keyCharacteristics: Evening ground everywhere; depth from tonal steps of one green and 1px inset lines, not from light sections or glow.
Coral is now and paid: the scrubbers, today, Paid, the received figure and the primary button. Ink on coral.
Mint is a quiet second signal for done (signed, approved, success), as text or a 12% tint, never a fill under text.
Refusal salmon (`err`) is the product's no: text and icons only.
Bricolage Grotesque on its width axis: condensed heavy statements, condensed light dates, full-width text.
Every product surface carries "Demo data" and the same job: Lumen Studio, Northwind Co, P-0018, INV-0042, $42,000.

rules.name: The Evening Ground Rule
rules.body: Every section sits on `ground`. Surfaces step up through `inset`, `panel` and `panel-2`; off-white is never a surface or section ground, only text and fills no larger than a chip or a progress bar.

rules.name: The Salmon Says No Rule
rules.body: A refusal or an invalid entry is told in `err`, as text, an icon or a 2px ring, on a calm `panel-2` or ground; never as a fill, never as a border on a row, and never for anything that is merely pending or overdue. Coral says paid, mint says done, salmon says refused.

rules.name: The Coral Is Now and Paid Rule
rules.body: Coral marks the current date and settled money, plus the one primary action. It is a fill carrying `ink`, or the scrubber's own marker and fill line; never coral text on the dark ground and never a decorative coral border.

rules.name: The Heavy Statement, Light Date Rule
rules.body: Statements are condensed (75 to 82%) at 740 to 760 with negative tracking; dates and signatures are condensed at 300; everything read or clicked is full width at 400 to 650 with no tracking.

rules.name: The Tabular Columns Rule
rules.body: Figures in columns, totals, tallies, money and rail dates carry `tabular-nums`; running copy does not.

rules.name: The Money Column Stays Rule
rules.body: On a phone a table holding money never drops a column: each row becomes a wrapped line with the name left and the amount right, the amount labelled from its column head, and the remaining columns as small `mut` meta prefixed with their own label. A non-money column (a date, a team) may be hidden; a figure may not.

rules.name: The Lines, Not Lifts Rule
rules.body: Containers are separated by tone and a 1px inset ring. A cast shadow belongs only to product windows; everything inside them and the sections around them stay flat.

rules.name: The Rows, Not Boxes Rule
rules.body: Inside an audience-page window nothing is boxed: panels, journal entries, chain rows, payment strips, messages, stamps and outcome blocks lose their fill, ring and radius and become rows under a 1px `line` top hairline. Rings stay only on controls (tool buttons, option tabs, the seat switcher trough, the URL bar, reaction pills). A not-yet row is a hairline row with a `mut-2` note, not a dashed box.

dos: Do keep every section on the evening ground and build depth from `inset`, `panel`, `panel-2` and 1px inset rings.
Do use coral for the current date and for settled money, plus the one primary button, always with ink text on it.
Do use mint as text or a 12% tint for signed, approved and success states.
Do set statements condensed and heavy and dates condensed and light in Bricolage Grotesque; keep reading text at full width.
Do set figures in columns, totals and money in tabular numerals.
Do make product state a function of the date, and give it a finished static form under reduced motion and without JavaScript.
Do tag every product surface "Demo data" and keep the one job's names and figures.
Do tell a refusal in `err` text and icons, and keep everything inside an audience window as hairline rows.
Do stack money tables on phones so every figure keeps its column and its label.
donts: Don't add a light section, or use off-white as a surface or section ground.
Don't set coral text on the dark ground or use coral as a decorative border; its lines belong to the scrubbers.
Don't add glow, neon edges, glass or hard offset shadows; cast shadows stay on the three product windows.
Don't add uppercase tracked labels or eyebrows above headings; labels are sentence case.
Don't let the hero's date numeral scale past 1.3x or compete with the H1.
Don't use a wink in a primary button label.
Don't fill or box a refusal, or use `err` for pending or overdue.
Don't drop a money column on a phone.
